title: Europe & Western World GK
description: 36 original questions on European and Western geography, landmarks, history, science, and culture (Multiple Choice & Free-Text).
author: QuizRooms

questions.prompt: Which river flows through the heart of London?
questions.explanation: The River Thames flows through southern England and central London.

questions.prompt: In which Italian city is the ancient Colosseum located?
questions.explanation: Completed in 80 CE, the Colosseum stands in central Rome.

questions.prompt: Which mountain range forms a natural arc across Switzerland, Austria, France, and northern Italy?
questions.explanation: Mont Blanc is the highest peak in the Alps.

questions.prompt: Which city is home to the Statue of Liberty?
questions.explanation: France gifted the Statue of Liberty to the United States in 1886.

questions.prompt: Which European country is shaped like a high-heeled boot on a map?
questions.explanation: The Italian Peninsula extends southeast into the Mediterranean Sea.

questions.prompt: Which sea separates southern Europe from North Africa?
questions.explanation: The Mediterranean connects to the Atlantic via the Strait of Gibraltar.

questions.prompt: In which French museum is Leonardo da Vinci's Mona Lisa displayed?
questions.explanation: The Louvre in Paris is the world's most visited art museum.

questions.prompt: Which North American waterfall sits on the border between Canada and the United States?
questions.explanation: Niagara Falls lies between Ontario and New York State.

questions.prompt: Which European country is famous for its windmills, tulip fields, and canals?
questions.explanation: Roughly a third of the Netherlands lies below sea level.

questions.prompt: Which playwright wrote 'Hamlet', 'Macbeth', and 'Romeo and Juliet'?
questions.explanation: Shakespeare was born in Stratford-upon-Avon, England, in 1564.

questions.prompt: What currency is shared by most European Union member states?
questions.explanation: The Euro became physical circulating currency in 2002.

questions.prompt: Which Greek temple dedicated to Athena overlooks Athens from the Acropolis?
questions.explanation: Built in the 5th century BCE, the Parthenon is an icon of classical architecture.

questions.prompt: Which European river flows through more countries (ten) than any other river on Earth?
questions.explanation: The Danube runs from Germany's Black Forest to the Black Sea.

questions.prompt: Which landmark canyon in Arizona was carved over millions of years by the Colorado River?
questions.explanation: The Grand Canyon reaches depths of over 1,800 meters.

questions.prompt: Which Spanish architect designed Barcelona's Sagrada Família basilica?
questions.explanation: Construction of the Sagrada Família began in 1882.

questions.prompt: Which European mountain range separates Spain from France?
questions.explanation: The Pyrenees stretch from the Bay of Biscay to the Mediterranean.

questions.prompt: Which 15th-century German inventor introduced movable-type mechanical printing to Europe?
questions.explanation: Gutenberg's press in Mainz revolutionized the spread of knowledge.

questions.prompt: Which strait separates Great Britain from mainland France?
questions.explanation: The Channel Tunnel runs beneath the Strait of Dover.

questions.prompt: In which city is the Brandenburg Gate located?
questions.explanation: The Brandenburg Gate is an 18th-century neoclassical monument in Berlin.

questions.prompt: Which U.S. national park became the world's first national park in 1872?
questions.explanation: Yellowstone spans parts of Wyoming, Montana, and Idaho.

questions.prompt: Which Nordic island nation sits directly astride the Mid-Atlantic Ridge?
questions.explanation: Iceland harnesses abundant geothermal energy from volcanic activity.

questions.prompt: Which Belgian city is widely considered the de facto capital of the European Union?
questions.explanation: Brussels hosts the European Commission and Council of the EU.

questions.prompt: Which Canadian province is predominantly French-speaking?
questions.explanation: Quebec City and Montreal are major cultural centers of Francophone North America.

questions.prompt: Which Roman-era wall was built across northern Britain in 122 CE?
questions.explanation: Hadrian's Wall marked the northwestern frontier of the Roman Empire.

questions.prompt: What is the longest river wholly within Europe?
questions.explanation: The Volga runs about 3,531 km through western Russia to the Caspian Sea.

questions.prompt: Which 1215 English charter established that the monarch was subject to the rule of law?
questions.explanation: King John sealed the Magna Carta at Runnymede in 1215.

questions.prompt: Which mountain in the Caucasus is the highest peak in Europe?
questions.explanation: Mount Elbrus rises to 5,642 meters in southern Russia.

questions.prompt: Which historic Moorish palace and fortress complex overlooks Granada, Spain?
questions.explanation: The Alhambra is celebrated for its intricate Nasrid stucco and tilework.

questions.prompt: Which European microstate is completely landlocked inside the Italian Peninsula and claims to be the oldest republic?
questions.explanation: San Marino traces its founding tradition back to 301 CE.

questions.prompt: Which 1648 series of peace treaties ended the Thirty Years' War and shaped modern European state sovereignty?
questions.explanation: Signed in Münster and Osnabrück, Westphalia established territorial sovereignty.

questions.prompt: Which astronomer published 'De revolutionibus orbium coelestium' in 1543 placing the Sun at the center?
questions.explanation: Copernicus initiated the heliocentric revolution in astronomy.

questions.prompt: Which North American Great Lake is the largest freshwater lake in the world by surface area?
questions.explanation: Lake Superior covers over 82,000 square kilometers.

questions.prompt: Which Norwegian explorer led the first expedition to reach the South Pole in December 1911?
questions.explanation: Amundsen's team reached the South Pole 34 days before Scott's expedition.

questions.prompt: Which Dutch city is home to the International Court of Justice?
questions.explanation: The International Court of Justice sits in the Peace Palace in The Hague.

questions.prompt: Which strait separates Sicily from mainland southern Italy?
questions.explanation: The Strait of Messina is barely 3.1 kilometers wide at its narrowest point.

questions.prompt: Which ancient Celtic-era stone monument stands on Salisbury Plain in England?
questions.explanation: Stonehenge's iconic sarsen stones were erected around 2500 BCE.
